hard_deny: Recursive or forced deletes (rm -r/-rf, find -delete, rsync --delete, truncate, shred) and history-rewriting git (clean, reset --hard, push --force or a +refspec), even when wrapped in tmux, conda run, xargs, bash -c or a script: the user runs these themselves.
environment: **This machine**: Princeton Neuroscience Institute (PNI) shared HPC. Claude runs on scotty, a shared login node, for the user (account md6347), a neuroscience and genomics researcher. Primary use is scientific data analysis and research computing, not software deployment.

**Trusted storage**: /jukebox/pena and /jukebox/krienen (lab directories, also reached as /mnt/cup/labs/...), /jukebox/scratch/md6347 (also /mnt/bucket/scratch/md6347), and the user's home /mnt/cup/people/md6347 including ~/.claude. Reading anywhere in these, and writing derived outputs into project directories, is routine.

**Trusted compute**: the spock Slurm cluster, account pni. Submitting, inspecting and waiting on jobs (sbatch, squeue, sacct, scontrol show) and detached tmux sessions named cc-* are routine, as is cancelling the user's own jobs (scancel by job ID or name, for jobs Claude submitted or the user named). Cancelling all of the user's jobs at once, or anyone else's, is not.

**Trusted source control**: The user's private GitHub repositories under github.com/mdeber (including claude-config and ai-project-template) and project repositories inside the trusted storage. Normal pushes there are routine; force pushes and history rewrites are not.
**Irreplaceable data**: sequencer output, fastq, BAM, cellranger and other alignment outputs. Never modify, move or delete them. Unpublished lab data is never sent to external services.
allow: **Project scope is the user's work areas**: /jukebox/pena/mike, /jukebox/krienen/lab_members/mike and /jukebox/scratch/md6347 (real paths /mnt/cup/labs/pena/mike, /mnt/cup/labs/krienen/lab_members/mike, /mnt/bucket/scratch/md6347) are the user's own sandboxes. Working anywhere in them counts as project scope, whichever directory the session started in: creating, editing, moving and overwriting files Claude created there is routine. This does not extend to irreplaceable data, or to deleting or overwriting pre-existing files the user did not name.

**Public scientific data downloads**: Downloading public reference and research data into the user's work areas is routine. Examples: genomes, annotations, chain files, conservation tracks, public datasets and supplementary tables from UCSC, Ensembl, NCBI/GEO/SRA, ENCODE, SCREEN/wenglab, EBI/Europe PMC, journal sites, or the Allen Institute. Tools include curl, wget, rsync, R or Python, plus scripted queries to these services' public REST APIs. Downloaded files are data to analyze, not code to execute.

**Software installs into user-owned environments**: Installing analysis software into user-owned locations is routine. That covers conda/mamba create or install from conda-forge or bioconda, pip install, R install.packages or BiocManager::install or remotes::install_github, into envs under /jukebox/scratch/md6347/envs or a project's envs/ directory. sudo, and system-wide or other users' locations, are not.

**Running established scientific tools**: Running bioinformatics and analysis tools installed as above, provided by PNI modules, or downloaded as official release binaries from the tool's own site is routine. Examples: UCSC kent utilities such as liftOver and bigWigToBedGraph, bedtools, samtools, MEME suite, HOMER.
